title: A reliable map from a property specification to a makeable material

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a reliable way to start with a desired material property and obtain a composition, atomic structure and experimentally executable recipe that produces a material with that property. It would connect inverse design—working backward from a requirement—with predictive synthesizability: determining whether a candidate can actually be made and under which processing conditions. Generating a plausible crystal structure, predicting low energy or successfully making a phase addresses only part of this chain.

Conceptual synthesis: a useful specification would state the property, its required magnitude and the conditions under which it must hold, together with relevant constraints on material form and processing. The output would need to describe how to obtain the material in that form, rather than merely identify an idealized arrangement of atoms. Reliability would mean prospective experimental success within a declared domain, with explicit uncertainty and boundaries. The supplied evidence does not demonstrate this complete capability across unrelated material classes.

significance.text: The revolutionary potential lies in closing the gap between proposing materials and obtaining useful specimens. The documented studies distinguish candidate selection from determining workable synthesis conditions. If a method reliably joined those tasks to experimentally verified property targets, it would provide a broadly useful framework for materials creation. Its direct consequence would be less trial-and-error route discovery and fewer unsuccessful synthesis attempts within its validated domain. This assessment of significance is a conditional inference from the documented technical gap.

Success across several classes would not establish that synthesis screening had ceased to be a rate limiter throughout equilibrium and near-equilibrium solids. A material's useful behavior can depend on microstructure, processing and device integration as well as phase identity. The A-Lab outlook explicitly treats microstructure and device performance as further objectives beyond synthesizability. Practical processing and scale would therefore remain part of assessing the innovation's reach.

Conceptual synthesis: reliable property-to-material design could accelerate the search for better structural, energy, catalytic and quantum materials wherever physically attainable candidates and workable processing routes exist. It would not guarantee that every requested property combination is possible. Discovering a new physical phenomenon, such as ambient-pressure room-temperature superconductivity, would remain a separate achievement. Faster interatomic potentials could improve the calculations supporting the map, but would not alone supply reliable synthesis planning or experimental property verification. No specific historical analogy is established by the supplied evidence.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central unsolved capability in this concept is predictive synthesizability integrated with property-driven design. A zero-temperature stability calculation can help screen structures, but low computed energy does not specify a successful synthesis route. Synthetic accessibility also depends on finite-temperature effects, entropy, reaction kinetics and processing history. A reliable method must connect those factors to the requested composition, structure and property, rather than assume that a favorable stability calculation makes the candidate experimentally accessible.

Concrete barriers documented in the A-Lab report include slow reaction kinetics, precursor volatility, amorphization and computational inaccuracy. These can prevent the target from forming even when calculations motivate attempting it. Disorder and competing phases further complicate the relationship between a predicted structure and the specimen obtained. The required advance must account for the route through which the material forms, including conditions that favor the target over alternatives.

Reliable characterization is another necessary component. In the retained A-Lab report, four additional automated product assignments became inconclusive after manual reexamination because the target diffraction patterns could not be distinguished adequately from those of other known phases using X-ray diffraction alone. This establishes ambiguity in the assignments; it does not establish that all four products were definitively misidentified. A learning system cannot be judged reliably if its experimental feedback confuses ambiguous phase assignments with confirmed successes.

Conceptual synthesis: the full breakthrough also requires transfer beyond familiar examples. A method must distinguish learning broadly useful synthesis relationships from retrieving close matches to materials already represented in training data. It must carry that reliability through to the specified property, including the effects of composition, disorder, material form and microstructure. The supplied studies document obstacles to this goal, but do not establish a complete account of the field's remaining barriers as of November 2026.

current_state.text: Szymanski et al., Nature 624, 86–91 (2023), describe an autonomous synthesis platform. The version evaluated in the supplied review is marked as updated in January 2026 and reports 36 realized compounds from 57 targets over 353 experiments. Approximately 63% of targets were eventually obtained, while only 30% of tested synthesis recipes produced their targets. Those measures answer different questions: eventual success after repeated attempts does not establish success on the first or second proposed route. The article states that its targets were new to the laboratory and absent from the training data used by its recipe-proposal algorithms; that exclusion does not by itself establish transfer to an untuned material class.

The retained A-Lab article header identifies an Author Correction published on 19 January 2026, and the retained PDF identifies a modified publication in 2026. The separate correction text is absent from the supplied review, so the numerical wording in this retained version cannot automatically be attributed to the original 2023 publication. Earlier counts in the peer-review material belong to manuscript history rather than a competing final result. The review used retained article text but did not visually inspect the figures or separate diffraction datasets, so the reported synthesis outcomes should not be read as independently revalidated product assignments.

Prein et al., arXiv:2511.01790v1, submitted on 3 November 2025, report seven successful target matches among 16 characterized samples. This is a preprint result. The full-text evidence summarized in the review shows that 24 targets were attempted: eight samples bonded strongly to their crucibles and could not undergo further characterization. Those eight outcomes are unresolved; inability to characterize them establishes neither successful target synthesis nor necessarily failed synthesis. The abstract's seven-of-sixteen result therefore describes the characterized subset rather than all attempted targets.

Prein's seven reported successes also do not mean seven new, held-out majority products. Three successful target-or-polymorph cases were subsequently found nearly identical to entries already labeled as synthesized and were effectively present in the training data. In one reported case, the target Y2MnFeO6 polymorph appeared at only 3.3% concentration. Together with the small, selected experimental set, these details limit conclusions about novelty, majority-phase production and transfer across unrelated chemistries. Although the review had full extracted paper text in addition to a partial landing-page copy, it did not visually inspect the diffraction figures.

The research notes attribute to Merchant et al., Nature (2023), graph-network predictions placing 2.2 million structures below the then-current convex hull, with 736 independently experimentally realized structures. The supplied review could not verify those figures: the retained PubMed artifact contained only a cookie challenge, without an identifying abstract or article content. These numbers therefore remain attributed research-note claims here. If the stated interpretation is accurate, the 736 figure concerns prior experimental realization rather than a closed prospective synthesis campaign; it would not establish that the model supplied and experimentally validated 736 successful routes.

The research notes also attribute to Leeman et al., PRX Energy 3, 011002, dated 7 March 2024, a categorical critique that the examined work discovered no new materials. No Leeman artifact was supplied for the review, so its identity, date, wording, evidentiary basis and relationship to the later corrected A-Lab account remain unverified here. The critique cannot resolve the novelty dispute on this record. Its absence is an evidence limitation, not evidence that the critique is false.

Evidence-bound synthesis: the reviewed results demonstrate substantial progress in automated synthesis and experimental testing of predicted materials, with important limits on route efficiency, characterization, training independence and the meaning of success. They do not demonstrate the complete property-to-composition-to-structure-to-route capability described here. The supplied freshness record contains no bounded search establishing field-wide status as of 1 November 2026. Consequently, these dated reports cannot support a claim that no later system has achieved broader capabilities.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: preregister several material classes, including at least one on which the method has not been tuned, and a prospective test set new relative to its training examples. Each case should start from a stated property target with defined measurement conditions and relevant constraints on material form and processing. The method should return a composition, structure and sufficiently detailed synthesis route for independent experimentalists to execute. Retrospective agreement with known crystals would not qualify as this demonstration.
completion_criteria.label: Prospective targets yield executable synthesis routes across preregistered material classes

completion_criteria.text: Proposed success criteria: independent experimentalists should obtain the predicted phase as the majority product on the first or second stated route and verify the requested property under the specified conditions. Sample sizes, the numerical success threshold and uncertainty reporting should be set before results are known. The threshold should make failed targets the exception, but no particular percentage is established by the supplied evidence. Target-level success and route-level success should be reported separately, with all attempted targets accounted for, including uncharacterized specimens.
completion_criteria.label: Independent synthesis yields majority target phase and specified property

completion_criteria.text: Proposed verification and reproducibility criteria: characterization should distinguish the target from competing phases and establish the relevant composition and disorder. Property measurements should test the resulting specimen in its declared form rather than infer performance from a calculated ideal structure. Independent laboratories should reproduce successful routes with documented processing conditions and tolerances. Training-overlap checks should include close structural or polymorph matches, and results should disclose unsuccessful attempts and ambiguous assignments.
completion_criteria.label: Independent laboratories reproduce characterized specimens and directly measured target properties

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundaries: a convincing claim should state the chemistries, property ranges, processing conditions, material forms and scales over which reliability has been demonstrated. Performance outside those boundaries should remain an extrapolation. Finite tests can establish demonstrated breadth and transfer to selected unfamiliar classes; they cannot establish literal universality. Evidence for laboratory specimens would also leave larger-scale manufacture and device integration to be demonstrated where those are part of the intended use.
completion_criteria.label: Claims of reliability stay within explicitly stated demonstrated boundaries

related_concepts.text: Roster-based conceptual synthesis: MAS-01, Ambient-pressure room-temperature superconductivity in a manufacturable solid, and MAS-10, Topologically protected quantum matter outside the dilution refrigerator, concern particular quantum behaviors and their operating conditions. MAS-04 could help identify and make candidate materials for those goals, but route prediction would not establish the required quantum phenomena. Conversely, discovering one such material would not demonstrate a reliable inverse-design method across unrelated chemistries.

Roster-based conceptual synthesis: MAS-02, Bulk structural solids that are both near their ideal strength and damage-tolerant; MAS-05, Structural solids that remain engineering materials after fusion-level atomic displacement; and MAS-09, Structural metals that fully recover from macroscopic fracture in service, specify distinct structural and service-performance outcomes. Their overlap with MAS-04 lies in designing compositions and processing routes that deliver those properties. Strength, damage tolerance, irradiation resistance and fracture recovery would each require direct testing under the relevant conditions; identifying a phase would not establish them.

Roster-based conceptual synthesis: MAS-06, Reversible solids that store energy at chemical-fuel specific energy, and MAS-08, An ambient catalytic solid that fixes nitrogen at industrial intensity, provide demanding functional targets for a possible property-to-material map. MAS-04 could support candidate and route discovery, while reversible energy storage and industrially intense nitrogen fixation would remain separate demonstrations. A successful material in either category would establish a particular outcome rather than general synthesis predictability.

Roster-based conceptual synthesis: MAS-03, General atomically precise covalent construction, concerns control over construction at the atomic level, while MAS-07, Programmable growth of load-bearing solids, concerns directing growth to produce structural material. Both overlap with MAS-04 through process control and the connection between fabrication history and final structure. They could supply ways to execute some predicted routes, but neither necessarily provides an inverse map from a property specification. MAS-04 could also succeed within a bounded domain using conventional synthesis without achieving general atomic precision or programmable structural growth. These remain distinct entries.

change_log.change: Preserved MAS-04's identity and expanded its explanation into the full property-to-composition-to-structure-to-synthesis capability.
change_log.reason: The title requires more than candidate generation or successful phase synthesis; property verification and material form are integral to the proposed innovation.

change_log.change: Replaced the categorical description of predictive synthesizability as the field's single missing piece with a documented technical gap and concrete barriers.
change_log.reason: The reviewed sources support limitations involving kinetics, disorder, finite-temperature effects and processing history, but do not establish field-wide status in November 2026.

change_log.change: Changed the assertion of automated diffraction misidentification to four assignments becoming inconclusive after manual reexamination.
change_log.reason: Ambiguity between target and competing diffraction patterns supports characterization uncertainty, not definitive misidentification.

change_log.change: Qualified the claim that the innovation would end synthesis screening as a rate limiter.
change_log.reason: Reduced trial and error follows within a validated domain; elimination of the bottleneck across equilibrium and near-equilibrium solids would require broader evidence, including processing, microstructure and scale.

change_log.change: Reported A-Lab's 36-of-57 result alongside 353 experiments and 30% recipe success, and identified the retained version's January 2026 update.
change_log.reason: Eventual target success differs from route efficiency, and the revised text cannot establish the exact wording or counts of the original 2023 publication.

change_log.change: Expanded Prein's seven-of-sixteen report to include 24 attempted targets, eight uncharacterized samples, training overlap and a 3.3% target concentration.
change_log.reason: The abstract denominator and success count do not establish seven novel, held-out majority products. Uncharacterized samples remain unresolved outcomes.

change_log.change: Preserved Merchant's numerical claims and Leeman's critique as explicitly unverified attributions, with their access limitations.
change_log.reason: The Merchant artifact was a cookie challenge and no Leeman artifact was supplied. Missing evidence does not justify either endorsing or rejecting the underlying claims.

change_log.change: Strengthened the proposed completion demonstration with property measurements, preregistered thresholds, sample sizes, characterization rules, training-overlap checks and independent replication.
change_log.reason: These additions connect the evaluation to the complete concept and make success assessable without presenting proposed criteria as established standards.

change_log.change: Added explicit boundaries on generalization and distinguished MAS-04 from every other supplied roster entry.
change_log.reason: Finite demonstrations establish bounded breadth, while specific material achievements and fabrication capabilities remain separate innovations.

unresolved_issues: Merchant's reported 2.2 million structures and 736 experimental realizations, including the precise meaning of the latter count, remain unverified because the retained artifact contains only a cookie challenge.
Leeman's identity, publication date, exact conclusion, supporting analysis and relationship to the corrected A-Lab account cannot be established from the supplied artifacts.
The separate January 2026 A-Lab correction text is absent, so the changes from the original 2023 publication cannot be reconstructed reliably.
The review did not visually inspect A-Lab's figures or separate diffraction datasets, or Prein's diffraction figures; individual product assignments have not been independently revalidated.
Eight Prein samples could not be characterized after bonding to crucibles; their synthesis outcomes remain unknown.
No supplied freshness search establishes field-wide status as of 1 November 2026 or excludes later demonstrations of broader capabilities.

The proposed benchmark still requires a justified numerical success threshold, adequate sample sizes, selected material classes, property tolerances and explicit practical boundaries before execution.
The supplied evidence does not establish a specific historical analogy for the innovation's potential impact.

brief.title: Materials made reliably to order
possible: A researcher could specify how a material must perform and under what conditions, then receive its ingredients, atomic arrangement and a workable recipe. The result would be a specimen that meets the requirement.
This could help people find better materials for structures, energy, catalysts that speed chemical reactions, and quantum technologies.
why: Materials researchers could spend less time discovering recipes by trial and error. Connecting predictions to reliable experiments would mean fewer unsuccessful attempts and a faster path from a promising idea to a useful specimen.

sources.who: Amil Merchant and colleagues at Google DeepMind and Google Research
sources.showed: Their learning models greatly expanded the set of crystal structures predicted to be stable. Some matched structures already made independently.
sources.quote: Of the stable structures, 736 have already been independently experimentally realized.
sources.cited_for: Computers can identify many promising atomic arrangements.
sources.not_established: Matching previously made structures does not demonstrate successful recipes generated and tested for new targets.

sources.showed: Their robotic A-Lab made 36 target compounds, using experimental results to revise recipes when attempts failed.
sources.quote: All target materials considered in this work are new to the lab, that is, not present in the training data for the algorithms it uses to propose synthesis recipes
sources.cited_for: An autonomous laboratory can connect predicted materials to experiments and improve recipes.
sources.not_established: Eventual synthesis does not establish reliable early success or delivery of a requested property.

sources.showed: This is a critique disputing whether the examined work discovered new materials.
sources.cited_for: Whether the products count as newly discovered materials is disputed.
sources.not_established: The critique does not establish a reliable path from a requested property to a makeable material.

sources.who: Thorben Prein and colleagues at Altrove and Technische Universität München
sources.showed: In a preprint, the team reported seven target matches after ranking predicted materials by how likely they were to be makeable and testing proposed recipes.
sources.quote:
samples strongly bonded to their crucibles during synthesis and therefore could not be
subjected to further characterization.
sources.cited_for: Predictions of whether materials can be made can help select experimental targets.
sources.not_established: The small, selected study included training overlaps and a trace target product; it does not establish broad reliability.

shown: A-Lab has combined recipe prediction, robotic experiments and feedback to make target compounds. But only 30% of tested recipes produced their targets. Repeated attempts can achieve eventual success without making the initial recipe reliable.

Prein and colleagues have also connected candidate selection to experimental recipes. Some reported successes closely matched training examples, and some attempted samples could not be characterized. These studies demonstrate parts of the path from a requested property to a useful material.
missing: A method must connect a requested property to ingredients, atomic structure and a recipe that reliably produces the desired specimen.
Recipes must account for reaction speed, processing history and competing products, beyond calculated stability.
Independent experiments must confirm both the material's identity and its requested property, including for unfamiliar material classes.

milestones.label: New property targets yield executable recipes across material classes
milestones.explanation: Tests registered in advance would have to yield executable recipes for new property targets across declared material classes, including an untuned class. This would test transfer beyond familiar examples.

milestones.label: Independent synthesis delivers mostly the target and its property
milestones.explanation: Independent experiments would have to produce mostly the target material and its requested property within two proposed routes, under preset success criteria. This would establish practical reliability with all attempts counted.

milestones.label: Independent laboratories reproduce confirmed materials and measured properties
milestones.explanation: Independent labs would have to reproduce recipes, distinguish competing structures and directly measure the specimen's property, with training overlaps and failures disclosed. This would establish reproducible success.

milestones.label: Reliability claims match demonstrated practical boundaries
milestones.explanation: Claims would have to state the demonstrated chemistries, properties, processing conditions, forms and scales. This would define where reliability holds and where manufacture or device integration still needs testing.

uncertain: What success threshold, sample size and property tolerances would justify calling the method reliable?
The outcomes of samples that bonded to their crucibles remain unknown.
How far can success transfer across unfamiliar chemistries and material forms?

page.title: Synthesis-aware inverse design of inorganic crystals
page.definition: A system takes property specifications and measurement conditions and returns a composition, crystal structure—the repeating atomic arrangement—and a synthesis recipe that produces a specimen meeting those specifications. Experimental validation establishes the material domain in which the system works.

goal.need: A-Lab’s corrected account reports 36 target compounds from 57 targets in 353 experiments over 17 days, while only 30% of recipes produced their targets. Prein et al.’s preprint reports seven target matches among 16 characterized samples from 24 attempts; eight samples could not be characterized. These results quantify the gap between proposing a material and obtaining it, before requiring a specified functional property.

figures.caption: Different denominators in A-Lab’s corrected synthesis results
figures.note: The campaign lasted 17 days. Eventual target success includes repeated recipe attempts.

completion.title: An independent laboratory makes a property-specified crystal using a system’s unmodified synthesis recipe.
completion.criterion: A fixed system receives a property specification, measurement conditions and specimen constraints for a crystal outside its training examples. It returns the composition, crystal structure and complete synthesis recipe. A laboratory independent of the developers executes the recipe without target-specific route development, identifies the proposed material and measures the property within the input tolerance. A further study repeats the synthesis and property measurement with newly collected data and obtains consistent results within uncertainty.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas; fallback capability test because no external end-to-end acceptance criterion was located.
completion.basis: Searches of MGI strategies, NSF DMREF solicitations, DOE inverse-design goals, NIST benchmarks, and standards and prize criteria found no end-to-end acceptance test or numerical reliability cutoff. This is a bounded demonstration connecting the stated design goal to an executable recipe and independent experimental confirmation. It does not certify reliability across material classes.

milestones.title: An automatically proposed recipe produces an inorganic target at more than 50% by weight.
milestones.criterion: An automatically proposed recipe produces an inorganic target as more than 50% of the product by weight, assessed by X-ray diffraction and Rietveld refinement, which fits a structural model to the diffraction pattern. A-Lab accepts ordered or partially disordered target structures. Its corrected account reports 36 of 57 targets in 353 experiments over 17 days. The correction published on 19 January 2026 leaves four further assignments inconclusive. Leeman et al.’s 2024 critique addressed the earlier novelty and diffraction claims.
milestones.set_by: A-Lab developers, Szymanski et al., published synthesis stopping criterion for air-stable inorganic powders; not a general materials standard.
milestones.threshold_quote: the target is obtained with a yield exceeding 50%

milestones.title: An inverse-designed crystal has an experimentally estimated bulk modulus within 20% of its target.
milestones.criterion: Apply MatterGen’s reported proof-of-concept comparison: synthesize a property-conditioned crystal and obtain an experimentally estimated bulk modulus within 20% of the requested value. Bulk modulus measures resistance to compression. Of four selected synthesis candidates, one yielded reported TaCr2O6. Against a 200 GPa target, the authors used the maximum of four estimates, 169 GPa; their reported summary was 158 ± 11 GPa. The estimates combine nanoindentation measurements with a calculated Poisson ratio of 0.30. This is a reported validation check, not a field-wide acceptance threshold.
milestones.set_by: Microsoft Research AI for Science and collaborators, MatterGen’s published experimental validation check; the 20% comparison was reported for TaCr2O6.
milestones.threshold_quote: synthesizing a generated material and measuring its property to be within 20% of our target

milestones.title: A further study replicates a designed material’s synthesis and property results within uncertainty.
milestones.criterion: A further study synthesizes the previously designed material, collects its own structural and property data, and obtains results consistent with the original study given measurement uncertainty. Apply the National Academies’ definition of replicability; it supplies no universal percentage tolerance or required number of laboratories. Replicating a material precedes testing whether an unchanged system can supply a complete recipe for a new property specification.
milestones.set_by: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine, Reproducibility and Replicability in Science, adopted definition of replicability; applied here to synthesis and property experiments.
milestones.threshold_quote: Replicability is obtaining consistent results across studies aimed at answering the same scientific question, each of which has obtained its own data.

not_found: No independent experimental replication of MatterGen’s TaCr2O6 bulk-modulus result was located.
Subsequent characterization outcomes for Prein et al.’s eight crucible-bound samples were not located.
